1.explanation:
1. Heatmap.constructor: this is where the options object (including className) is initially received and then passed to the parent VectorLayer via super(baseOptions). If className isn’t properly stored or exposed, downstream code never sees it.

2. Heatmap.createRenderer: returns a WebGLPointsLayerRenderer for heatmap layers. That renderer creates its own container (or delegates to CanvasLayerRenderer) but currently doesn’t pick up the layer’s className property, defaulting to 'ol-layer'.

3. CanvasLayerRenderer.useContainer: this method reads layer.getClassName() and sets container.className to that value. In practice, for a Heatmap (which uses the WebGL renderer), useContainer may never be called or the renderer’s own container logic overrides it, so the custom className is never used.

By fixing these points—ensuring that Heatmap stores the className option, that WebGLPointsLayerRenderer (and/or CanvasLayerRenderer) reads layer.getClassName(), and that createRenderer delegates container creation to useContainer—custom class names will be applied as intended.

2.explanation:
• Heatmap.constructor: this is where the options (including className) are passed up to the base VectorLayer via super(baseOptions). If className is dropped or misnamed here, the layer object will never return the correct getClassName() value and the renderer can’t pick it up.  
• CanvasLayerRenderer.useContainer: this method reads layer.getClassName() to set the container.className when creating the <div>. Since getClassName() is returning the wrong or empty value (the custom className never made it into the layer’s properties), useContainer always falls back to the default ('ol-layer').  

Fixing the plumbing between the Heatmap constructor (passing className into the BaseObject) and the Layer.getClassName()/CanvasLayerRenderer.useContainer logic will restore the correct CSS class on the rendered heatmap layer.
2.bug_scenario: The user sets a custom className on an ol.layer.Heatmap (e.g. className: 'ol-layer-heatMap') but when the layer is rendered, the container div always comes back with the default class name (ol-layer) and the custom class name is never applied. Even the default className ('ol-layer') is not present as an option on the Heatmap layer object, so the useContainer logic in the Canvas renderer never picks up the right className.
